question:
Gandhi Cloth Company is capable of manufacturing three types of clothing: shirts, shorts, and pants. The manufacture of each type of clothing requires that Gandhi have the appropriate type of machinery available. The machinery needed to manufacture each type of clothing must be rented at the following rates: shirt machinery, $200 per week; shorts machinery, $150 per week; pants machinery, $100 per week. The manufacture of each type of clothing also requires the amounts of cloth and labor as shown in the following Table 1. Each week, 150 hours of labor and 160 sq yd of cloth are available. The variable unit cost and selling price for each type of clothing are shown in Table 2. Formulate an LP whose solution will maximize Gandhi's weekly profits.

Table 1 (The amount of labor hours and cloth required for each type of clothing):
| Clothing Type | Labor Hours | Cloth (sq yd) |
| ------------- | ----------- | ------------- |
| Shirt         | 3           | 4             |
| Shorts        | 2           | 3             |
| Pants         | 6           | 4             |

Table 2 (Revenue and Cost Information for each type of clothing):
| Clothing Type | Sales Price | Variable Cost |
| ------------- | ----------- | ------------- |
| Shirt         | $12         | $6            |
| Shorts        | $8          | $4            |
| Pants         | $15         | $8            |

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # Products
    "products": ["shirt", "shorts", "pants"],
    # Resources
    "resources": ["labor", "cloth"],
    # Resource availability per week
    "labor_available": 150,   # hours
    "cloth_available": 160,   # sq yd
    # Resource usage per unit produced: usage[resource][product]
    "usage": {
        "labor": {"shirt": 3, "shorts": 2, "pants": 6},
        "cloth": {"shirt": 4, "shorts": 3, "pants": 4},
    },
    # Machinery rental cost per week (fixed cost if product is made)
    "rental_cost": {"shirt": 200, "shorts": 150, "pants": 100},
    # Sales price per unit
    "price": {"shirt": 12, "shorts": 8, "pants": 15},
    # Variable cost per unit
    "var_cost": {"shirt": 6, "shorts": 4, "pants": 8},
    # Big-M: an upper bound on production of any single product
    # (limited by the tightest resource: labor 150/2 = 75 for shorts)
    "big_m": 150,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Sets
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])
    model.R = pyo.Set(initialize=d["resources"])

    # Decision variables
    # x[p] >= 0 : number of units of product p produced per week
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # y[p] in {0,1} : 1 if machinery for product p is rented (product is made)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: maximize weekly profit
    # profit = sum_p (price_p - var_cost_p) * x_p - sum_p rental_cost_p * y_p
    def obj_rule(m):
        revenue = sum(
            (d["price"][p] - d["var_cost"][p]) * m.x[p] for p in m.P
        )
        fixed = sum(d["rental_cost"][p] * m.y[p] for p in m.P)
        return revenue - fixed

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Resource constraints: sum_p usage[r][p] * x_p <= availability[r]
    def resource_rule(m, r):
        avail = d["labor_available"] if r == "labor" else d["cloth_available"]
        return sum(d["usage"][r][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= avail

    model.resource_limit = pyo.Constraint(model.R, rule=resource_rule)

    # Linking constraints: x_p <= big_m * y_p  (rent machinery to produce)
    def link_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= d["big_m"] * m.y[p]

    model.link = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=link_rule)

    return model

    "cloth": {"shirt": 4, "shorts": 3, "pants": 4},

    # Table 2: sales price -> "Sales Price" column
    "price": {"shirt": 12, "shorts": 8, "pants": 15},
    # Table 2: variable cost -> "Variable Cost" column
    "var_cost": {"shirt": 6, "shorts": 4, "pants": 8},

    # Rental rates per week: "shirt machinery, $200 per week; shorts machinery,
    # $150 per week; pants machinery, $100 per week."
    "rental": {"shirt": 200, "shorts": 150, "pants": 100},

    # "Each week, 150 hours of labor and 160 sq yd of cloth are available."
    "labor_avail": 150,
    "cloth_avail": 160,

    # Big-M: max units producible of any single product from labor or cloth limits.
    "big_M": 160,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets ---
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])

    # --- Variables ---
    # x[p]: units of product p manufactured per week
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # y[p]: 1 if machinery for product p is rented (product is made), else 0
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # --- Objective: maximize weekly profit ---
    def obj_rule(m):
        revenue_minus_vc = sum(
            (d["price"][p] - d["var_cost"][p]) * m.x[p] for p in m.P
        )
        rentals = sum(d["rental"][p] * m.y[p] for p in m.P)
        return revenue_minus_vc - rentals

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # Labor availability
    def labor_rule(m):
        return sum(d["labor"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["labor_avail"]

    model.labor_limit = pyo.Constraint(rule=labor_rule)

    # Cloth availability
    def cloth_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cloth"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["cloth_avail"]

    model.cloth_limit = pyo.Constraint(rule=cloth_rule)

    # Linking: production of p only if machinery rented
    def link_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] <= d["big_M"] * m.y[p]

    model.link = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=link_rule)

    return model
